title: Measurement: Surface Area and Volume
summary: Surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres, combined objects, and the effect of multiplying dimensions by a factor $k$.

notes.latex: V = \text{area of base} \times h \qquad \text{Cylinder: } V = \pi r^2 h, \quad A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h
notes.caption: Volume of a right prism; volume and total surface area of a cylinder

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: $H$ is the **perpendicular height** (used for volume); $h_s$ is the **slant height** (used for surface area). They are linked by Pythagoras: for a cone, $h_s^2 = r^2 + H^2$.

notes.title: Worked example 1: a cone
notes.problem: A cone has radius 6 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm. Calculate its volume and total surface area. Leave answers in terms of $\pi$.

notes.title: Worked example 2: a combined object
notes.problem: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius 3 m and height 10 m topped by a hemisphere. Find its volume, correct to one decimal place.

headers: If every dimension is multiplied by $k$…

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: The radius of a sphere is doubled. What happens to its volume?
steps: $k = 2$, so the volume is multiplied by $2^3 = 8$.
